subject.title: fix(gateway): regenerate native hook descriptors when relay unavailable after restart

question: Should an app-server approval whose native PreToolUse relay fails before invocation fall back to generic OpenClaw before-tool policy, or remain blocked until the relay is refreshed?
rationale: Both choices are technically possible, but they define the security behavior when native relay transport and generic policy evaluation disagree or when trusted-policy and loop-detection coverage differs.

options.title: Approve fallback after live proof
options.body: Accept the guarded fallback only after exact-head restart evidence shows generic policy, trusted policy, loop detection, and approval prompts still enforce correctly.

options.title: Require relay refresh
options.body: Keep relay-unavailable approvals fail-closed and re-register or refresh the relay before continuing tool execution.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Leave the current fail-closed behavior in place until a single canonical restart-recovery design replaces the competing fallback approaches.

recommendation.title: Approve fallback after live proof
recommendation.body: Accept the guarded fallback only after exact-head restart evidence shows generic policy, trusted policy, loop detection, and approval prompts still enforce correctly.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged guarded fallback defines the current unknown-unavailable behavior, and CODEOWNERS identifies them as the strongest available owner for this boundary choice.
